In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diet composition (protein and carbohydrate content) and ration size on intermediary metabolism in gilthead sea-bream (Sparidae) fed for 22 d with a high carbohydrate diet.

the effects of ration size and dietary protein and carbohydrate levels on the activities of enzymes involved in intermediary carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism of gilthead seabream (Sparaus aurata).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a high carbohydrate level in the diet stimulates the activity of enzymes of glycolysis and the pentose phosphate shunt and inhibits alanine aminooxidase activity, while a high protein level in the diet increases the activity of the key enzyme of lipogenesis.
the enzymes studied in Sparus aurata liver are good candidates to be used as indicators of nutritional status in fish.
the activities of key metabolic enzymes are highly responsive to changes in diet composition and ration sizes in cultured fish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the enzymes 6-PFK, pyruvater kinase, G-6-PD, and G-6-PDH, which are key enzymes in glycolysis-glycogenolysis, pentose-phosphate pathway, and gluconeogenesis, can be used as a marker for growth and ration size, but not for diet composition.
diet type and ration level are important factors for the regulation of enzyme activities involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and proteins.

the enzymes of Sparus aurata liver are sensitive to changes in ration size and diet composition, and that these responses may be used as a tool in the study of the metabolic adaptation of cultured fish.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fish are able to respond rapidly to dietary manipulations by changing the activity of key enzymes in liver.
the enzyme activities of Sparus aurata liver are very responsive to dietary manipulations and ration size, suggesting that these fish are very adaptable to changes in their diet and ration size.

the enzymes of the glycolytic pathway and the pentose phosphate shunt are stimulated by a high carbohydrate diet, while the enzymes involved in lipogenesis, amino acid catabolism and gluconeogenesis are stimulated by a low carbohydrate diet.
